review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: SQL namespaces and identifiers; query descriptions, execution and results; ordinary/materialized views; plans, scans and join algorithms; constrained column sets; relational algebra as a formal query language.
review.attribution: Open English WordNet 2025 candidate review continues with the notices in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. PostgreSQL 18, SQLite and the Illinois Institute of Technology relational-algebra tutorial support technical extensions missing from the general dictionary. Qualified labels, intersections and graph mappings are editorial adaptations. Source prose and SQL examples are not copied.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U3 with unspecified strength. Preserve old home contexts; expose the existing general plan genus in U3 rather than duplicate it. Constraints and their column sets are distinct; algorithms and execution are distinct.

sense_decisions.scope: A naming scope for information objects; not physical space.
A named namespace grouping database objects; distinct from a description of database structure.
A lexical name identifying an SQL object; no database-independent case-folding policy.
The delimited identifier form using double quotes; not a string literal.
The unquoted lexical identifier form; reserved-word rules depend on the SQL implementation.
A compound object name including its schema qualifier; not a single identifier token.
A specification requesting database data, distinct from executing it or sending a network message.
A complete SQL SELECT statement specifying retrieval; not its running execution.
Data returned by a database retrieval query; not the query text, plan or execution.
A query result with a tabular structure; duplicates are not excluded.
A named tabular view defined by a query, with ordinary and materialized forms distinguished below.
An ordinary view whose defining query supplies rows when referenced; no separately maintained view-row storage.
A query-defined view with persisted results; those results need not be current.
The retained definition of a query-defined view, separate from its result rows.
Recomputing the contents of a materialized view using its definition; no automatic scheduling or incremental implementation is assumed.
An executable strategy described as plan nodes; not the execution itself or a guaranteed fastest strategy.
One described operation within a query plan, distinct from running that operation.
Producing a query execution plan from the query specification.
Software that evaluates candidate plans and chooses a plan under its cost model.
Executing a data-retrieval query, distinct from planning and representing the request.
A successfully completed retrieval execution producing a result, which can be empty.
Execution of a database access operation; not its plan node.
Scanning table data as a database access operation.
Traversing a database index for data access; no universal speed advantage or heap-access rule.
Executing a join over tabular inputs; distinguish the operation from the selected join algorithm.
An algorithm for implementing a database join.
A join algorithm based on hash lookup of join keys.
A join algorithm traversing inputs ordered on their join keys; sorting need not be a separate step.
A selected collection of columns from a table; distinct from a column value or a constraint.
A column set containing one column; not identified with the column itself.
A column set containing multiple columns.
The local referencing columns of a foreign key; they need not uniquely identify local rows.
The columns designated as a table primary key; not the constraint rule or an index.
A foreign-key column set with one local column.
A foreign-key set spanning multiple local columns.
A primary-key set spanning multiple columns.
Preserve schema description; namespace is a separate meaning.
Preserve the existing foreign-key rule and introduce its constrained column-set meaning separately.
Reuse nested loops as an algorithm rather than creating a duplicate from a different capitalization.
Tuple remains queued; no SQL row is asserted to be an ordered mathematical tuple merely by a common database label.
Correct the query-language classification; relation and operator semantics need a separate detailed cohort.
A query description is not automatically a network request.
Use a query-defined view family with materialized and nonmaterialized restrictions; do not force stored results onto ordinary views.
The everyday optimization gloss promises rendering optimal; technical query planning only selects under its cost model.
The dictionary opinion/view homonym is unrelated to a database view.
The dictionary cognitive schema is unrelated to a database namespace.

review.limits: No database schema or application data is changed. Namespaces are not schema descriptions. Materialized views are not universally current, automatically refreshed or faster. No optimal-plan guarantee, mandatory index scan, foreign-key uniqueness, mandatory external-table reference, candidate-key minimality or universal case-folding rule is added. Relational algebra is corrected in its query-language reading; its operator family and tuple/set semantics remain queued. Existing generic querying probabilities are preserved without recalibration.

exclusion_review.decision: Keep clear scans and preserve upper exclusions and explicit negations; distinctions do not require new universal exclusions.

review.collision_decision: No new normalized-term collisions accepted. Reuse the plan, nested-loop algorithm, constraints and relational-algebra records. New technical senses use qualified terms.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
